title: Separate association proposals from authorized acceptance
summary: Make candidate association an explicit decision boundary. An evaluator can propose a connection, while the neutral engine checks revisions, permissions, and protected dispositions before accepting it.
implementation: Represent candidate IDs/revisions, alternatives, evidence, matching-rule version, and proposal status.
Build exact-key proposals and accept external semantic proposals without trusting their claimed authority.
Require a current candidate-set revision and permitted acceptance policy.
Retain rejection and correction history so replay cannot silently reattach a rejected association.

acceptance.criterion: No-match, ambiguous, and insufficient-evidence outcomes stay distinct.
acceptance.verification: Test zero candidates, two plausible candidates, and unavailable key evidence.

acceptance.criterion: A stale candidate proposal cannot be accepted.
acceptance.verification: Race an identity update against proposal acceptance.

acceptance.criterion: Relatedness and confidence do not confer merge or override authority.
acceptance.verification: Submit high-score proposals against protected dispositions.

tests: A new matching candidate invalidates prior uniqueness.
Attachment acceptance can coexist with merge refusal.
A protected separation survives replayed proposals.
risks: A score field may be mistaken for permission to mutate identity.

reuse.application: Adapt conflicting-match handling while keeping proposals separate from accepted decisions.
